_comment: Five real NASA (and NASA-partner) missions for the Mission Health tab. Every fact has a link in that mission's 'sources' list; 'dataset' points to the matching data.nasa.gov dataset where one exists. 'kind' is 'real' for flown missions and 'simulation' for ground analogs, and the page shows that label. active_profile is null: no mission runs until the crew starts one on the Mission health page.

crew13_iss.label: Crew-13 · ISS Expedition 75
crew13_iss.where: International Space Station, low Earth orbit
crew13_iss.radiation: About 80–160 mSv over a 6-month ISS stay (NASA 2017 figure), still inside Earth's magnetic shield.
crew13_iss.summary: A six-month science expedition on the ISS. Microgravity is the main threat: bones, muscles, heart and eyes all change when nothing pulls you down.

sources.title: NASA: Crew-13 launches to the ISS
NASA: The Human Body in Space
NASA: Five hazards of human spaceflight

twin_study.label: NASA Twin Study · One-Year Mission
twin_study.where: International Space Station (Scott Kelly) vs. Earth (Mark Kelly)
twin_study.radiation: Inside Earth's magnetic field on the ISS, but for almost a year, roughly double a normal expedition.
twin_study.summary: One twin spent 340 days in space while the other stayed home. Ten research teams compared their genes, immune systems, eyes, arteries, gut bacteria and thinking.

sources.title: NASA: Twins Study results published in Science

dataset.title: Multi-omics analysis: mitochondrial stress in spaceflight (uses Twin Study data)

artemis2.label: Artemis II · Crewed lunar flyby
artemis2.where: Around the Moon on a free-return path, beyond Earth's magnetic field
artemis2.radiation: Deep-space radiation through the Van Allen belts and beyond, tracked by 6 cabin sensors and a dosimeter in each crew member's pocket.
artemis2.summary: The first crew to leave Earth orbit since 1972. Short trip, but a campervan-sized capsule, deep-space radiation and no quick way home.

sources.title: NASA: Artemis II crew both subjects and scientists
CSA: Artemis II science during the mission

mars520.label: Mars-520 · Simulated Mars round trip
mars520.where: Sealed habitat at IBMP Moscow (ESA and Russia's Institute of Biomedical Problems)
mars520.radiation: None: a ground simulation. It tested the mind, not radiation or weightlessness.
mars520.summary: Six people lived 520 days in sealed modules acting out a full Mars trip: 250 days out, 30 on the 'surface', 240 back, with up to a 20-minute message delay.

sources.title: Basner et al., PNAS 2013 (sleep and activity)

dataset.title: Epigenetic patterns during the Mars 520-d mission simulation

spacewalk.label: Spacewalks (EVA) · US & Russia
spacewalk.where: Outside the ISS, in a pressurised suit
crew: Hundreds of US astronauts and Russian cosmonauts (see the EVA dataset)
spacewalk.radiation: Only a suit between the astronaut and space, so less shielding than inside the station.
spacewalk.summary: Hard physical work in vacuum inside a stiff, pressurised suit. NASA lists spacewalks among the most dangerous things astronauts do.

sources.title: NASA: Risk of injury from EVA
